promptState.text: This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon 3D render of a small robot bunny mech character in a Pixar-like style, with chibi proportions: a big round head and a short, chunky body. It stands full body, facing the viewer. It is built from glossy white armor plates with bright orange panels, has two mechanical bunny ears with orange tips, big round glowing cyan eyes on a dark face visor, chunky robotic arms and legs with silver joints, and the word "PIXA" printed in bold white letters on its orange chest plate. There is empty space above its ears and below its feet. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.

{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt.
  • Load VAE - Turns the finished render into a picture. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can make transparent pictures.

 The speed node

Teal, above the graph.

  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. The note on the right has the numbers. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Pick Orientation and Size - The size of the picture. The starred sizes are the native 2K sizes Qwen lists for this model; the others are smaller and much faster. For video, 1920 x 1088 is Full HD (the model works in steps of 16 pixels, so 1080 becomes 1088) and 2560 x 1440 is 1440p. The orientation switch flips a size between portrait and landscape.
  • 2. Add a prompt - What you want to see, between two fixed sentences. The first one, This is an RGBA image with transparency., and the last one, The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent., are what make the background transparent: keep them, and change only what is between them. Put any words you want written on your subject in quotes, like "PIXA" in the demo prompt.
  • 3. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same picture, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt through the text encoder. It has a negative prompt box, but that does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • Empty Latent Image - The blank canvas, at the size from step 1.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from ComfyUI's own template.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the picture and saves it to your output folder as a PNG, which keeps the transparency. In the preview, the transparent part shows the node's own dark grey.

The dark Run Timer above it shows how long the last Run took. Handy when you are trying sizes against the table in the other note.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

A subject on a transparent background, straight from a prompt: here, a cartoon robot bunny. Qwen Image 2.1 draws the transparency itself, so there is no background to remove afterwards. The picture is saved as a PNG, ready to place on another picture, in a design or in a video.

Tested on 10 seeds with the demo prompt: every one came out with a transparent background, the whole bunny inside the picture and "PIXA" spelled right.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How the background becomes transparent

Two sentences do it, Qwen's own wording from the model card. The prompt starts with the first and ends with the second, and your subject goes between them:

This is an RGBA image with transparency. [your subject]. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.

Leave them out and you get a normal picture with a background: the demo bunny without the two sentences came out on a solid background on all 4 seeds tried, with no transparent pixel at all.

Describe only the subject, never a place. In the first tests, the words soft studio light put a floor line under the feet on one seed and a reflection on another, so the demo prompt has no light or place words at all.

Keep the subject inside the picture: a character tends to fill the frame, and an ear cut off at the edge stays cut off in the PNG. The last sentence of the demo prompt, There is empty space above its ears and below its feet., is there for that. On the same 10 seeds without it, one bunny had its ear tips cut off at the top edge; with it, none.

 The edges and the purple

Under the transparent part the picture is a flat purple. You never see it in a PNG, but anything that throws the transparency away, like saving as JPG, will show it.

The soft edges are clean: on the 18 test pictures of the demo prompt, placed on white, not one of the 214,546 edge pixels showed any purple. And the background really is empty: away from the bunny, nothing was more than 4 out of 255 opaque on 9 of the 10 seeds, far too faint to see; the tenth had a faint soft shadow under the feet.

In the preview the transparent part shows the node's own dark grey. To see the transparency, open the PNG from your output folder in an image editor: it comes in as a layer with the background already gone.

 How long a Run takes

SizePixels25 steps
832 x 1248 (the default)about 1 MP5 s
1024 x 1024about 1 MP5 s
1088 x 1920Full HD, about 2.1 MP10 s
1536 x 1536about 2.4 MP12 s
1440 x 25601440p, about 3.7 MP21 s
1696 x 2528native 2K, 4.3 MP27 s

The two sentences cost no time: on the same seed at 832 x 1248 the demo prompt took 5 s, and the same subject without them 5 s.

The picture's size is what costs you. Work out your subject at the size this workflow opens on, then switch to a starred size for the picture you keep.

 Video sizes: Full HD and 1440p

Full HD is 1088 x 1920 in portrait and 1920 x 1088 in landscape. The model works in steps of 16 pixels, so 1080 is not possible: asking for 1080 gives exactly the same 1088 picture. For an exact 1080, trim 8 pixels. 1440p, 1440 x 2560 or 2560 x 1440, divides evenly and comes out exact. Tests at both sizes came out with the background just as transparent.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at 1696 x 2528, it took 27 s, against 39 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out as the same bunny in the same pose, with small differences in the fine details, like the lines on the helmet. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder. Measured on an 832 x 1248 picture: 9 s with the models unloaded first, 5 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 21 GB during these runs, at 1696 x 2528. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 More ideas

  • The same two sentences work for other subjects too: in earlier tests they gave a fox sticker, a mug and a robot a transparent background. Keep the words about the subject only.
  • The Text to Image + Prompt Enhancer workflow in this folder can write these prompts from a short idea: click the gear on its AI Prompt node and load the preset Qwen Image 2.1 - transparent picture from an idea.
  • To cut a subject out of a picture you already have, use the Remove Background workflow in the One Image Edit folder.
